heroHeadline: Bamako Siege Day 20: IRC Activates Emergency Response; JNIM Issues Djibo Return Warning; AES Joint Air Campaigns Ongoing; Togo Heightens Northern Border Security
heroSubtitle: Bamako enters Day 20 of JNIM's declared total siege — the International Rescue Committee activated an emergency humanitarian response for Mali as the WFP field suspension holds and food prices stay doubled (rice +43%, bread +55–65%). All four JNIM siege vectors remain simultaneously active: road interdiction (3 of 6 corridors), Manantali power grid sabotage, Kenieroba prison pressure, and supply convoy arson. JNIM-aligned Ansaroul Islam leader Ousmane Dicko released a video calling on Djibo civilians to evacuate military-adjacent areas — the clearest signal yet of a planned second assault on the provincial capital overrun for 9 hours on May 11. Togo activated elevated security posture along its Savanes Region northern border following the fall of Diapaga (May 13) — the last FAB buffer just 25 km from Togolese border towns. The AES Unified Force continues joint air campaign operations confirmed across Malian territory. The EU has pledged €151.28 million in 2026 Sahel humanitarian assistance; the FAO projects 52.8 million people at acute food insecurity risk in the June–August lean season.
